summary: A 1919 Aermotor steel tower on Hurricane Mountain near Keene, NY; closed in 1979, spared in 2010, open to hikers by 2015, roof needing replacement at the 2018 NHLR visit.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the peak has hosted a fire tower since 1909. The Explorer, citing the Friends of Hurricane Mountain website, dates the first observers to 1910. The story gives both dates.

NHLR visit reports conflict. The 2017 report marks the tower as staffed, but its comments describe volunteer interpreters. The 2007 and 2018 reports list it as unstaffed. The story treats it as unstaffed for fire watch and reports the conflict.

sources.title: Tower lighting pays homage to fire observers

notes_for_editor: Brief build year 1919 confirmed. The start of fire watch is 1909 (NHLR) or 1910 (Friends via Explorer). Staffing records conflict across NHLR visits. The 2010 reclassification comes from Adirondack Life. A Daily Gazette piece gives 2014 for a St. Regis Mountain parcel, not Hurricane, so it is not used here. Pure Adirondacks is a hiking blog for the 2015 reopening; current access was not verified. The last NHLR visit is March 2018, so the roof and condition may have changed. The NRHP nomination (npgallery d62496c9) was not read. Revised on fact-check 2026-10-08: 'Today' now reports the 2018 visit findings; the well-signed trails claim is footnoted; the 1979 closure is attributed to the Friends group; the removal of the Primitive-land tower is no longer presented as caused by its land classification.
